name: Constructive learning
description: Algorithms that build network structure during learning rather than fixing architecture in advance.

name: Candidate-unit training
description: Training possible additions before deciding which unit should be installed.

name: Residual-error correlation
description: Selecting new units by how strongly their activations correlate with remaining output error.

name: Frozen features
description: Stabilizing learned structure by freezing some weights after installation.

name: Hidden-unit growth
description: Increasing representational capacity by adding hidden neurons.

name: Capacity control
description: Adjusting model size to match task complexity.

name: Backpropagation
description: Gradient-based credit assignment used either as a base learner or as part of growth.

name: Historical foundations
description: Early work that set up later constructive neural network methods.

name: Modular composition
description: Building complex functions by composing smaller learned modules.

name: Incremental structure
description: Architectural growth performed in steps rather than all at once.

name: Growth trigger
description: The signal or criterion that decides when a constructive learner should add new capacity.

name: Spiking neural networks
description: Neural-network models where spikes and their timing are first-class signals rather than hidden implementation details.

name: Spike-timing-dependent construction
description: Constructive algorithms whose growth, pruning, or parameter-selection processes depend on spike times.

name: Parameter calculation
description: Processes that assign useful initial parameters to newly constructed neurons or synapses.

name: Local performance trigger
description: Growth or pruning decisions driven by the assessed performance of individual components rather than only global error.

name: Simulation expansion
description: Interpreting construction as moving neurons or synapses from an unsimulated surrounding system into the simulated set.

name: Structural plasticity
description: Creation, deletion, or reconfiguration of neurons and synapses during learning or simulation.

name: Pruning and merging
description: Capacity-control operations that remove components or combine similar components rather than only adding new ones.

name: Topology constraints
description: Cases where the structure produced by a growth rule limits what the resulting network can represent or learn.

name: Recurrent structure
description: Constructive methods for sequence models where recurrence, memory dynamics, or finite-state behaviour shape the growth rule.
